text:
AI Engineering Toolkit!

I have curated a list of 100+ LLM libraries and frameworks for training, fine-tuning, building, evaluating, deploying, RAG, and AI Agents.

Categories of LLM Libraries include:

• Vector Databases – Store and retrieve embeddings efficiently.
• Orchestration & Workflows – Chain tools and LLM calls, manage pipelines.
• Agent Frameworks – Build autonomous and multi-step agents.
• Training & Fine-Tuning – Pretrain, fine-tune, and adapt models.
• Inference & Serving – Run LLMs efficiently on diverse hardware.
• Safety & Security – Guardrails, red-teaming, and policy checks.
• Evaluation & Quality – Test and monitor both LLMs and LLM-powered apps (benchmarks, unit tests, telemetry, feedback).
• Model Management – Versioning, experiment tracking, lineage, and lifecycle management.
• AI App Development – Build UIs and LLM-powered apps quickly with Python-based frameworks.

Your next data role depends on more than just knowing SQL.

Here’s a complete step-by-step breakdown of the interview stages — and exactly how to prepare for each one 👇

🔹 𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟭: 𝗥𝗲𝗰𝗿𝘂𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗖𝗮𝗹𝗹 (~𝟯𝟬 𝗺𝗶𝗻𝘀)
🎯 Goal: Evaluate experience, skills & communication.
💼 How to Prepare:
• Craft a 30-sec pitch (who you are, what you do, what you're looking for)
• Share 2–3 stories showing impact
• Use relevant keywords (SQL, Python, BI tools, etc.)

🧪 𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟮: 𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 (~𝟲𝟬 𝗺𝗶𝗻𝘀)
🎯 Goal: Test SQL & business interpretation
💡 Topics to Cover:
• SQL Basics: GROUP BY, JOIN, etc.
• Ranking: RANK(), DENSE_RANK()
• Window Functions: LAG(), LEAD()
• Business case questions: metric drops, feature suggestions, KPIs

📦𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟯: 𝗧𝗮𝗸𝗲-𝗛𝗼𝗺𝗲 𝗔𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 (~𝟭.𝟱 𝗵𝗿𝘀)
🎯 Goal: Analyze real-world dataset + make recommendations
📊 What you'll do:
• Clean & explore data
• Visualize insights
• Suggest next steps
🧠 Showcase your problem-solving and storytelling skills.

🏢 𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟰: 𝗢𝗻-𝗦𝗶𝘁𝗲 𝗼𝗿 𝗙𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 (~𝟰–𝟱 𝗵𝗿𝘀)
🎯 Goal: Dive into SQL + business & behavioral rounds
💬 Be ready to answer:
• A project you're proud of
• How you manage workload/conflict
• Strategy-level impact you've had

✅ 𝗧𝗼𝗽 𝗦𝗸𝗶𝗹𝗹𝘀 𝘁𝗼 𝗠𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿:
1️⃣ Communicate projects clearly

3️⃣ Define the right metrics

author: Sachin M
headline: Sr. Tech Consultant-Analytics@GyanSys | Ex-Deloitte
text:
SQL 15/50 ( KPMG SQL Interview Problem)
Problem statement: 
Find and remove duplicate rows from a table based on specific columns, keeping only one unique row per duplicate group.

Input table: 

Customers

| customer_id | name | email |
|-------------|-----------|-----------------------|
| 1 | John Doe | john.doe@email.com |
| 2 | Jane Smith| jane.smith@email.com |
| 3 | Mike Jones| mike.jones@email.com |
| 4 | John Doe | john.doe@email.com |

SQL query (using CTE and ROW_NUMBER to keep one row per duplicate group): 

WITH CTE AS (
 SELECT *,
 ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY name, email ORDER BY customer_id) AS rn
 FROM Customers
)
DELETE FROM CTE WHERE rn > 1;

Output table after removal: 

| customer_id | name | email |
|-------------|-----------|-----------------------|
| 1 | John Doe | john.doe@email.com |
| 2 | Jane Smith| jane.smith@email.com |
| 3 | Mike Jones| mike.jones@email.com |
